A.explanation: This adds all three e.m.f.s, which would only be correct if $V_1$, $V_2$ and $V_3$ all drove current in the same sense round the loop.

B.explanation: This makes $V_1$ and $V_2$ aiding and only $V_3$ opposing, but the diagram shows $V_2$ opposing $V_1$.

C.explanation: This makes $V_1$ and $V_3$ aiding and only $V_2$ opposing, but the diagram shows $V_3$ opposing $V_1$.

D.explanation: Going round with current $I$, $V_1$ is traversed from $-$ to $+$ while $V_2$ and $V_3$ are traversed from $+$ to $-$, giving $V_1 - V_2 - V_3 = I(R_1+R_2+R_3)$.

hints: Trace the marked current $I$ round the single loop through $R_1$, $V_2$, $R_2$, $R_3$, $V_3$ and $V_1$ and note the total resistor drop $I(R_1+R_2+R_3)$.
Compare the way the three cells are connected: $V_1$ is oriented to push current in the direction of $I$, while $V_2$ on the left and $V_3$ on the right are oriented the opposite way.
Apply Kirchhoff's second law round the loop in the direction of $I$: add an e.m.f. as $+V$ when going from $-$ to $+$ and as $-V$ when going from $+$ to $-$, then equate to the resistor drops.
walkthrough: Identify the loop and direction: the current $I$ flows left through $R_1$ at the top, down through $V_2$ on the left, right through $R_2$ and $R_3$ at the bottom, and up through $V_3$ and $V_1$ on the right.
State the rule: Kirchhoff's second law says the algebraic sum of e.m.f.s round a closed loop equals the sum of the $IR$ drops, so $\sum V = I(R_1+R_2+R_3)$ with signs.
Check $V_1$ at the top: traversing in the direction of $I$ goes from its $-$ side to its $+$ side, so it supplies energy and contributes $+V_1$.
Check $V_2$ on the left and $V_3$ on the right: traversing in the direction of $I$ goes from $+$ to $-$ for each, so they absorb energy and contribute $-V_2$ and $-V_3$.
Combine the signed e.m.f.s: $V_1 - V_2 - V_3 = I(R_1 + R_2 + R_3)$. This is option D.
